title: Filings and the Certified Auto Policy: Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing Position Statement
content:
## Position

Every Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing certifies one Cardinal Personal Auto Policy, and all filings on a policy follow that policy:

1. When the policy is cancelled for any reason, nonrenewed or expires unpaid, an SR-26 is transmitted for every accepted filing on it where the certificate's SR-26 switches for that ending are set to send one.
2. When the policy is reinstated, every filing on it that is still cancel-notified (an SR-26 sent and not yet in effect) is restored.
3. The policy's financial-responsibility indicator stays on while any filing on the policy is requested, filed, accepted, rejected or cancel-notified, and is switched off when the last of them is released or lapses.

## What this means at the policy level

- **All filings move together.** A policy carrying certificates for two drivers sends an SR-26 for each accepted certificate when the policy ends, and restores each one still cancel-notified when the policy is reinstated. No filing on the policy is left behind.
- **The indicator reflects the filings, not the policy alone.** The indicator turns off only when no filing on the policy remains in any of the five statuses listed above.

## Indicator table

| Filings on the policy | Financial-responsibility indicator |
|---|---|
| At least one requested, filed, accepted, rejected or cancel-notified | On |
| Every filing released or lapsed | Off (switched off when the last of them is released or lapses) |

## Hypothetical illustration

A policy carries two filings, one accepted and one rejected. The policy is cancelled for nonpayment: an SR-26 is transmitted for the accepted filing (the certificate's switch for nonpayment cancellations is set to send one). The indicator stays on, because both filings remain in listed statuses. When the rejected filing is later released and the other lapses, the indicator is switched off.
